subject: Canary model sweep — temporary capacity exemption request
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Canary model sweep — capacity ask

Team —

Product is planning a controlled canary: a 48-hour model-sweep to validate quality delta for the new 70B variant across three tokenizer configs and two quantization modes (6 configs x 10 seeds approximate). We expect bursts of short-lived generation jobs (avg seq len ~120 tokens) and need stable latency to evaluate A/B metrics.

Ask: can Infra provision an ephemeral Dedicated pool with the following constraints for this experiment:
- 4 x A100-80GB (logical GPU units pinned) for 48 hours (2026-12-18 09:00 UTC start)
- Autoscaling min override: keep min=1 node so the canary maintains warm KV caches (exception to standard min=0 policy)
- Region: us-west-2 only
- Rate limit per-client: 10 concurrent requests

Rationale: we want deterministic perf for the eval — without pinned warm capacity KV cache churn will dominate latency noise and invalidate the sweep. We understand this is an exception to autoscale economics; attached is a short plan and a cost estimate.

Attachments: canary-plan.pdf (plan + success metrics)

If we can get an approval path this week we'll queue the pool creation and run validation tests before end of next week.

TL;DR: 48h ephemeral Dedicated pool (4 GPUs), autoscale min=1 exception, us-west-2.

Thanks,
Laura
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-15T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Canary model sweep — capacity ask

Laura —

Quick questions and a couple of constraints from Infra:
- Autoscale min override is doable for a short window but we need an explicit rollback time and a tagging convention so billing shows up to the product cost center.
- If the workload is very bursty we can suggest a burst lane (pre-provisioned ephemeral buffer) rather than forcing min=1 for the whole 48h. Burst lane would let us spin up to 6 GPUs for short windows and tear down to 0 when idle — lower cost but more KV cache variability.
- Need expected token throughput per second and expected concurrent sessions to validate scheduling and packing heuristics.

Can you paste the expected RPS and token/sec? Also confirm whether the experiment can tolerate a soft fallback to quantized variants if a GPU goes OOS.

Dev
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-16T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Canary model sweep — capacity ask

Thanks for surfacing this — marking a couple of trade-offs and a proposal so we can move to a decision:

Trade-offs:
- Fixed min=1 for 48h gives the cleanest latency signal (warm KV caches) but is cost-inefficient if utilization is low between runs.
- Burst lane keeps cost down but may reintroduce cache-warm jitter.

Proposal:
1) Approve a constrained exception: Create an ephemeral Dedicated pool of 4 GPUs (us-west-2), start 2026-12-18T09:00Z, duration 48h.
2) Policy controls: autoscale min override to 1 only for the pool, enforced tag product:canary-2026-12-18, and an automatic rollback at 2026-12-20T09:30Z if not manually extended.
3) Instrumentation: route the canary through a per-route telemetry tag so Console shows token-level cost and latency by model variant (INFRA-2431).
4) Cost safety: cap burn to $X,000 (see attached cost-estimate.csv) and require code-owner sign-off before extend.

Next steps I need from Product: exact expected RPS / token/sec and confirmation whether tolerating soft fallback to 8-bit variants is acceptable. Also please confirm you want KV warm caching prioritized (we'll pin memory).

If Product signs off here I'll own the approval and task infra to provision the pool + add the rollback automation.

—Rishi
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: ops@starlabs.ai <ops@starlabs.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-17T09:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Canary model sweep — capacity ask

Hi Rishi / team,

We are an external partner helping coordinate GPU spot inventory for the week. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- Are you requesting guaranteed reserved capacity (billing as Dedicated) or do you want our market-backed buffer (preemptible with a 30m eviction tolerance)?
- If reserved, we'll need a Doc ID to attach to billing and an internal acceptance timeline (we require 48h lead time for guaranteed reservations on p4/80s).

Also, please confirm whether cross-region fallback is allowed. If us-west-2 is saturated we can fall back to us-west-1 or us-east-1 but that will force rerouting and invalidate some of the latency comparisons.

Ops
Starlabs Cloud Ops
